The unlawful homicide committed abroad by a minister of country X is a jure imperii act, because killing in the exercise of state power is sovereign conduct, not a commercial one. The territorial tort exception (UN Convention on Jurisdictional Immunities, Art. 12) does not apply, since it covers only acts occurring in whole or in part in the forum state. The ICJ in *Germany v. Italy* (2012) held that jus cogens violations do not remove state immunity.
